title: Canonical streaming-tokenization guardrails for multiplexed uploads and rate-limited reconnects
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: We observe intermittent double-charging and misattribution when clients upload multipart/streamed payloads that are reconnected/resumed under different tokenizer versions or when the rate-limiter injects backpressure and causes out-of-order fragments. This ticket implements a canonicalization + provisional-ledger pattern so the metering pipeline treats in-flight speculative output separately until a deterministic commit point is reached.

Background: Current pipeline assumes stable tokenization per session and deterministic ordering of frames. In practice: (1) clients may re-encode the same logical prefix using different tokenizer rules (tokenizer v1 vs v2) which leads to token-count divergence; (2) reconnects or proxying can cause fragment reorder or duplicates; (3) speculative decoding or early flush can create provisional outputs that later get supplanted. These scenarios cause duplicated debits or orphaned prefix charges.

Goal: Prevent double-charging and ensure deterministic final attribution for streaming sessions while preserving low-latency streaming and the ability to service rate-limited clients. Provide an implementation that: (a) is backwards-compatible with existing session protocol, (b) keeps latency SLOs (no full-stream re-tokenization on the hot path), and (c) produces auditable ledger entries that can be reconciled offline.

Non-goal: This ticket does not change billing unit semantics (we remain per-token), nor does it fully rework client SDKs — client SDK changes are optional for improved telemetry but server-side protections must be sufficient on their own.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress canonicalization layer emits deterministic token-span mapping (canonical_span_id) for every incoming fragment
Provisional ledger entries are written for speculative outputs and only converted to committed charges after a server-side checkpoint/commit token
Replays, duplicate fragments, and out-of-order fragments are deduplicated against canonical_span_id and idempotency token
Telemetry exposes per-session mismatches (client_tokenizer_fingerprint != server_fingerprint) and reconciliation delta summaries
Automated fuzz + replay test harness demonstrates zero double-charges across 10k synthetic reconnect scenarios
Rollout plan with canary (5% requests) and automatic rollback on >1% unexpected charge deltas
proposed_solution: 1) Ingress canonicalizer: when a fragment arrives attach a canonical_span_id computed from (session_id, fragment_index, normalized_text). Normalization uses Unicode NFC + whitespace collapse + server tokenizer fingerprint mapping to a canonical token span without full token decode on hot path (use byte-span heuristics + small tokenization cache).

2) Provisional ledger: write speculative debits to a provisional ledger namespace (provisional_{session}) with a TTL. Each provisional entry references canonical_span_id and an idempotency_token computed from (origin_connection_id, client_nonce, sequence_number).

3) Commit handshake: when a fragment boundary is acknowledged or an explicit commit event occurs (end-of-message or server-side stable checkpoint after KV-cache warm), convert provisional entries into committed charges and emit final audit record. If a conflicting canonical_span_id mapping is later received, keep the committed mapping if commit timestamp precedes conflict; otherwise write a compensating adjustment entry and emit reconciliation alert.

4) Rate-limiter/backpressure interaction: when applying backpressure that causes reordering, preserve the original client sequence numbers in the provisional ledger and ensure idempotency checks use (client_seq, origin_connection_id). Avoid re-tokenizing for reordered fragments by matching normalized_text fingerprint and canonical_span_id cache.

5) Tokenizer-version mismatches: store client-supplied tokenizer_fingerprint in session metadata. If mismatch detected, mark the provisional entries as 'needs_reconciliation' and attempt server-side deterministic re-tokenization in background reconciliation job. If re-tokenization cannot reconcile within TTL, generate compensating adjustment rather than charging twice.

6) Observability: add metrics and traces for provisional vs committed counts, reconciliation delta (tokens_compensated), and async-job success rates. Provide a console dashboard and an audit API to surface the provisional window for a session.

7) Tests: extend the existing shotgun fuzz harness to generate reconnects, tokenizer-version flips, and proxy-induced reorders. Add golden-record replay tests against recorded production traces (sanitized).
tradeoffs_and_risks: Extra write amplification: provisional ledger doubles writes for hot fragments; mitigated by compaction and short TTLs (default 10m).
Slightly more complex reconciliation path: requires careful compensation logic to avoid stale refunds; will add e2e invariants and a reconciliation FSM in code review.

Latency: canonicalization must avoid a full tokenization pass on the hot path — we use heuristic byte-span + small LRU tokenization cache. There is a small risk of mismatch leading to background reconciliation load.
Edge-case: malicious clients could spam mismatched tokenizer fingerprints. Mitigation: per-session heuristic limits and mark for manual review if reconciliation delta spikes.
implementation_tasks: A. API: add fragment-level canonical_span_id and idempotency_token fields to ingress API and wire through proxy layers (compatibility-safe: if absent, server computes).
B. Storage: provisional ledger sharded by session_id with compact commit log. Implement compactor that atomically converts provisional -> committed entries.
C. Reconciliation service: background worker to reconcile 'needs_reconciliation' provisional sets with deterministic server re-tokenization; emits compensating adjustments when necessary.
D. Rate-limiter integration: ensure rate-limiter adds origin_connection_id and preserves client_seq metadata on delayed resends.
E. Tests: unit + integration + fuzz harness updates; record-and-replay tests against sanitized production samples.
F. Telemetry: new metrics, logs, and console dashboard. Add a small dashboard tile for provisional_ratio and tokens_compensated.
G. Docs + runbook: short runbook for operations (how to inspect provisional ledger, run reconciliation manually, perform compensating entries).
test_plan: 1) Unit tests: canonical_span deterministic mapping invariants, idempotency checks.
2) Integration: simulated proxy reorder + reconnect flow with assert(no_double_charge) across permutations.
3) Fuzz: extend current harness to 10k scenarios with randomized tokenizer fingerprints and reorder patterns; assert final ledger total == ground truth token count.
4) Shadow rollout: run canonicalization + provisional logging in shadow mode for 48h on 100% traffic, monitor provisional_ratio and reconciliation load.
5) Canary: enable provisional->commit on 5% traffic, monitor financial deltas, then 25% and full rollout if stable.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag off; deploy canonicalizer and provisional ledger in shadow mode. 48h monitoring.
Phase 1: Canary (5%) with automatic rollback threshold: >1% unexpected charge delta or >0.5% increase in average tail latency.
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% over 3 days each, with reconciliation job scaled appropriately.
Phase 3: Post-rollout 7-day audit comparing provisional->committed deltas to historical baselines and runbook sign-off.
observability_and_alerts: Metric: provisional_to_committed_ratio per region and per model (alert if > 0.2 sustained over 10m)
Metric: tokens_compensated_rate (alert if > 50 tokens/min per tenant)
Trace: sample full session flows including canonical_span_id mapping for manual inspection
Runbook: steps to revert provisional ledger compaction and perform manual compensation adjustments
comments: 2026-02-18 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after investigating multiple customer reports of duplicate charges during network flakiness. Included initial prototype notes and example traces.
2026-02-22 - Luca Moretti: Reviewed; pushing for minimal hot-path work. I'll prototype LRU token-span cache and provisional ledger schema. Blocked by shard key decision for ledger storage.
2026-02-25 - Priya Shah (SRE): Verified that provisional writes at current QPS would add ~4% storage and suggested compaction strategy. SRE OK with short TTLs.
2026-03-03 - Engineering review: Design RFC posted (link below). Agreed to attach client_tokenizer_fingerprint to session metadata in SDKs as optional enhancement.
2026-03-09 - QA: Added fuzz harness tests; initial run (2k scenarios) shows 0 double-charges in shadow mode. Expanding to 10k.
2026-03-10 - Product: PM reviewed and approved canary thresholds; requested that billing team be notified at start of canary.
notes: Implementation will aim to be compatible with existing console audit API; we'll add provisional view as an opt-in column.
If reconciliation job is overloaded we will increase TTL and queue pacing; limits configurable per-tenant.
We should coordinate with billing ops for notification and manual reconciliation tools prior to Phase 1 canary.
